title: Machine learning guides Fe–Mn–Ni catalysts for NOx reduction
summary: An artificial neural network trained on literature data and a genetic algorithm helped identify Fe–Mn–Ni catalyst compositions for ammonia selective catalytic reduction. Researchers synthesized and tested model-guided candidates and report good NOx conversion for Fe₀.₃₁₉Mn₀.₂₀₆Ni₀.₄₇₅ over the tested temperature range. The work combines model selection, human screening and controlled experiments; the ratio is not a complete oxide formula and does not demonstrate industrial exhaust performance. The article text differs on whether the workflow involved two or four iterations, so this summary avoids an iteration count.
ai_technology: Artificial neural network and genetic algorithm
organization: State Environmental Protection Key Laboratory of Integrated Surface Water-Groundwater Pollution Control, Southern University of Science and Technology

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full text, PubMed metadata/affiliation and publisher date chronology.

evidence.tested: The paper reports synthesis and catalytic conversion testing of selected Fe–Mn–Ni formulations.
evidence.unknown: Article reports inconsistent iteration counts; test range and lab results do not establish durability or practical flue-gas performance.
evidence.ai_role: An ANN and genetic search ranked candidate Fe–Mn–Ni compositions; experimental results were used in the iterative optimization workflow.
